content.title: About
content.content: Wheat biscuit is a baked product made from wheat flour, sugar, butter, and often additives such as leavening agents, vanilla, or spices. It has a crisp or soft texture, a mildly sweet flavor, and is commonly enjoyed as a light snack or accompaniment to tea and coffee.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wheat biscuits originated in Europe in the 19th century and quickly became popular due to their simple preparation.
There are many variations: with raisins, nuts, chocolate, or spices.
Traditionally biscuits are baked as round or square pieces, but modern shapes can be any geometry.
Biscuits are often used as a base for dessert layers, such as in tiramisu.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Wheat biscuits provide quick‑acting carbs that rapidly replenish energy.

items.title: Contains some fiber
items.content: When made with whole‑grain flour, biscuits can contribute to digestive health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour supplies thiamine, niacin, and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Biscuits contain iron, magnesium, and phosphorus, supporting various bodily functions.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: High amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat biscuits contain gluten and are unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Some recipes use partially hydrogenated oils, which contain trans fats harmful to heart health.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Biscuits may contain nuts, eggs, or dairy, which can trigger allergic reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Biscuits can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, served with tea, coffee, or milk, used in dessert layers, crumbled into yogurt or ice cream. For a healthier option, choose whole‑grain biscuits without added sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store biscuits in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent mold growth and maintain crispness.

content.title: About
content.content: Dessert pizza is a sweet pastry, usually with a thin crust, topped with cream, fruit, berries, chocolate or nuts. It combines the crunchy base of a traditional pizza with a variety of dessert toppings, making it a popular treat for parties and family meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first dessert pizza was served in Italy in the 1970s as an experimental twist on classic pizza.
There are many variations: berry sauce, caramel, Nutella, ricotta cheese, and even ice‑cream topped versions.
Dessert pizza is often presented as a "pizza‑cake" with multiple layers of dough alternating with cream and fruit.
In Japan, a popular "mochi pizza" replaces the dough with a sweet rice cake base, topped with fruit and sweet paste.
Sweet pizza is believed to keep children more engaged than a regular dessert because of its interactive presentation.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The crust and sweet toppings provide carbohydrates that quickly replenish glycogen stores.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Fruits and berries used as toppings are rich in vitamin C, potassium and antioxidants.

items.title: Calcium from ricotta
items.content: Ricotta or mascarpone, commonly used in dessert pizzas, are good sources of calcium.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Sweet flavors stimulate serotonin production, helping to lift mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Toppings often contain nuts, dairy or gluten, which may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The crust and creamy toppings make dessert pizza calorie‑dense; portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve dessert pizza warm or at room temperature. Cut into serving slices, add fresh berries, dust with powdered sugar or drizzle with chocolate sauce. It pairs well with ice cream or whipped cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the finished pizza in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in the oven for 5‑7 minutes before serving to restore a crisp crust. Frozen pizza can be stored for up to 1 month, wrapped tightly in plastic film and foil.

content.title: About
content.content: Fried fish (NS) is fish that has been cooked by deep‑frying in oil at high temperature. The product features a golden crust, a fragrant aroma, and tender meat inside. It is commonly used in fast‑food dishes, snacks, and as a standalone meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Frying intensifies the aroma and creates a crispy texture.
Fish with firm flesh such as cod, hake or sea bass are often chosen for frying.
The tradition of batter‑fried fish comes from European cuisine, while plain dry frying is popular in Russia.
Fried fish is frequently served with sauces: tartar, mayonnaise, soy sauce.
In some countries it is sold as street food – the classic fish‑and‑chips.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Fish provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Despite frying, some omega‑3s remain, supporting heart and vascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Fried fish contains vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It supplies selenium, iodine and phosphorus, which aid thyroid function and bone health.

items.title: Easy digestion
items.content: Thermal processing makes the protein more readily digestible.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Frying increases calories and saturated fat, which may be undesirable in excess.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: High‑temperature frying can produce acrylamide, a potential carcinogen.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Certain fish species can contain mercury or cadmium; choose reputable suppliers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried fish can be enjoyed on its own, served with potatoes, rice or vegetable sides. It pairs well with lemon, fresh herbs, and a variety of sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fried fish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a bag at –18 °C, where it retains quality for up to 2 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Orange juice 100 % is a natural juice made from ripe oranges, enriched with calcium. It is available in cans, bottles, and carton packs. The drink provides vitamin C, flavonoids and other micronutrients, while the added calcium supports bone health.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Calcium is added in a micro‑crystalline form that is easily absorbed by the body.
The juice can be stored for up to 12 months in a sealed container at room temperature.
Orange juice is widely used in cooking: for marinades, sauces and cocktails.
Unlike many fruit juices, this product contains no added sugar.
Carton packaging is made from recyclable materials and protects the juice from light.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity, supports collagen synthesis and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Added calcium helps maintain bone density and reduces the risk of osteoporosis.

items.title: Contains flavonoids
items.content: Flavonoids have anti‑inflammatory and cardiovascular protective effects.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The juice is almost entirely water, contributing to proper fluid balance.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: One cup (250 ml) provides about 110 kcal, making it suitable for diet plans.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to oranges.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although no sugar is added, natural sugars may affect blood glucose levels.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Calcium can reduce the absorption of certain antibiotics and iron, so take them at different times.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the juice chilled, use it in smoothies, cocktails, sauces and marinades. For optimal calcium absorption, pair it with vitamin D‑rich foods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 5 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Barbecue-flavored potato chips are thinly sliced potatoes fried to a crisp and coated with a smoky, sweet‑savory spice blend that mimics the taste of barbecue. They are a popular snack often enjoyed at movies, picnics, and as a quick bite.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial potato chip brand appeared in the early 1920s in the United States.
Barbecue flavor is achieved with smoked paprika, sugar, onion, garlic, and a mix of spices.
Depending on the cooking method, chips can contain up to 30% fat.
In Russia, barbecue chips are often confused with “smoked bacon” flavored chips.
There are low‑calorie baked versions where the potatoes are oven‑cooked instead of fried.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Chips provide carbohydrates that deliver quick energy, useful during travel or active events.

items.title: Vitamin C content
items.content: A small amount of vitamin C remains in potatoes, especially when chips are cooked at lower temperatures.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potatoes are a good source of potassium, which helps maintain fluid balance.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Excess salt can raise blood pressure, so moderation is recommended.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: Because of fat and carbs, frequent consumption may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Some recipes include dairy or soy additives that can trigger allergic reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy chips straight from the bag, use them as a crunchy topping for sandwiches, salads, or incorporate them into dishes like baked vegetables for added texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep chips in a sealed bag or airtight container in a cool, dry place away from light. After opening, consume within 1–2 weeks to retain crispness and flavor.

content.title: About
content.content: A taco is a Mexican dish consisting of a corn tortilla filled with chicken, beans, and cheese. The whole‑grain corn tortilla provides a light base, while the chicken, beans, and cheese make the dish hearty and nutritious.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tacos are traditionally served in small portions, allowing you to try several different fillings.
Corn tortillas have been used in Mexico for over 3,000 years.
Beans in tacos are a good source of plant protein and fiber.
The cheese commonly used is cheddar or queso fresco, which melts easily.
Typical toppings include salsa, guacamole, and a squeeze of lime.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken and beans provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Beans and whole‑grain corn tortilla supply dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Using lean chicken and moderate cheese keeps saturated fat levels modest.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken and beans are sources of vitamin B6 and folate, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces and cheese can be high in sodium; those with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Tacos can be calorie‑dense, especially with generous cheese and sauces; portion control is advised.

items.title: Food‑borne bacteria
items.content: Chicken must be fully cooked to avoid the risk of salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Warm the tortilla, fold it in half with the filling, and add fresh salsa, guacamole, sour cream, or lime to taste. For a lighter version, use whole‑grain tortillas and reduce the amount of cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Tacos are best eaten immediately. If needed, store them in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Keep tortillas dry in a cool place, and store raw ingredients (chicken, beans) in the fridge at ≤ 4 °C.

content.title: About
content.content: The toddler meal “Pasta and Vegetables” is designed for children from 1 year old. It consists of finely cut whole‑grain pasta, gently cooked vegetables (carrot, broccoli, zucchini) and a small amount of vegetable oil. The dish is rich in carbohydrates, vitamins and minerals needed for growth and development.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole‑grain pasta provides more fiber than regular white pasta.
Vegetables are steamed, preserving up to 90 % of their vitamins.
The meal contains no added sugar or salt, meeting WHO recommendations for infant nutrition.
Each serving is sized at 120 g of ready‑to‑eat product – an optimal amount for a small stomach.
The product is packaged in a sealed, freezer‑safe pouch for convenient storage.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Whole‑grain pasta supplies sustained energy, supporting a child’s activity levels.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and B6 aid protein and carbohydrate metabolism, promoting healthy nervous system development.

items.title: Contains vitamin C and beta‑carotene
items.content: Carrots and broccoli provide antioxidants that strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: A modest amount of calcium from the vegetable oil contributes to bone formation.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion and helps maintain a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: Some children may be sensitive to gluten; in such cases a gluten‑free alternative should be used.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Vegetables and pasta must be fully softened to prevent blockage of the airway.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The dish contains minimal salt, but parents of children with hypertension should consult a pediatrician.

items.title: Storage
items.content: After opening, keep the product refrigerated and consume within 48 hours.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the portion in the microwave or on the stove to about 37 °C, stir with a fork until smooth, and serve immediately. If desired, add a small amount of infant‑appropriate dairy product.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened packages in a cool, dry place at 0 °C to +25 °C. Once opened, keep the pouch sealed in the refrigerator. When frozen, the product retains quality for up to 3 months.
